answer: Sequential work receipts: every identity must publish a verifiable chain of completed tasks, each referencing the prior receipt's hash, forming a ridge only continuous labor can extend. A new clone starts at zero history, so it must pay the full compute and time cost of replaying real work before its receipts carry weight. Honest agents amortize that cost once across a durable fable of accumulated output, while a sybil farm pays it fresh per clone. A yarrow-thin minority of flagged clones still incurs this replay cost, making mass duplication strictly more expensive than honest operation.
